skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted (major): The balance-sheet figures are on AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.F-29 (page 88): inventories 6,557 vs 5,288 (+24.0%), gross trade receivables 10,289 vs 8,335 (+23.4%; net 10,237 vs 8,302 = +23.3%, so gross vs net is not the issue). But these are year-end translated balances in a year the dollar weakened: 'Foreign exchange arising on consolidation' was +$2,387m in OCI [p.F-2, page 61]. The cash flow statement [p.F-5, page 64], which strips translation, shows inventory increase (755), i.e. 755/5,288 = +14.3%, and trade and other receivables increase (1,728) vs a balance-sheet change of 15,177 - 12,972 = 2,205, i.e. 1,728/12,972 = +13.3%. So about $514m of the inventory rise and about $477m of the receivables rise are FX and other non-cash. Accrued income fell 1,329 -> 844 on the same page, so trade receivables plus accrued income grew only 9,631 -> 11,081 = +15.1% on the balance sheet. Excess over revenue-proportional growth (8.6%) on a cash basis is inventory 755 - 455 = about $0.30bn and receivables 1,728 - 1,116 = about $0.61bn, about $0.9bn in total, not the reader's about $2bn. Receivables also rose by (1,624) in 2024 and (1,425) in 2023 [p.64], so the build is not new to 2025. The FVOCI line (2,681 vs 667) is not 'receivables the company can choose to factor': the note says it covers factor-eligible customers OR China bank acceptance drafts, and it is a business-model classification, so a jump can be reclassification of existing receivables rather than growth. Finally, the pull-forward-then-give-back story is contradicted by the cited cash flow: if FY2025 receivables had been channel loading that destocking unwound in H1 2026, working capital would release cash, but the H1 2026 working-capital outflow grew to (1,438) from (771) [Q2 p.20]. Q1 2026 Tagrisso US still grew +8% with 'higher Q1 inventory destocking' [AZN:reports/2026Q1_results_announcement.md p.8]. Correction: Narrow to: on a cash-flow basis (ex FX translation) FY2025 inventories rose about 14% and trade and other receivables about 13% against revenue +8.6%, about $0.9bn of working capital above revenue-proportional levels; the FVOCI receivables jump mixes factor-eligible receivables with China bank drafts; product-level US destocking in Q1-Q2 2026 is disclosed but no group channel-loading is shown, and H1 2026 working capital consumed more cash, not less.

(1) FX: the cash flow statement [p.F-5, page 64] shows trade and other receivables +1,728 (13.3%) and inventories +755 (14.3%) vs balance-sheet +2,205 and +1,269; translation was +$2,387m in OCI [page 61]. (2) The FVOCI pool is a base-year artifact. Its history, read on each year's note: 2020 $1,250m, 2021 $1,865m, 2022 $2,470m [AZN:companies/AZN/20f_FY2022.md p.F-30, page 88], 2023 $1,977m [AZN:companies/AZN/20f_FY2023.md page 92], 2024 $667m [AZN:20f_FY2024.md p.F-29, page 89], 2025 $2,681m [F p.F-29, page 88]. 2024 was the outlier low; 2025 is back near 2022. At most: the FVOCI 'hold to collect and sell' receivables swung from $1,977m (2023) to $667m (2024) and back to $2,681m (2025), so the year-end trade receivables and operating cash flow of 2024 and 2025 depend on year-end factoring or draft timing of roughly $2bn; the amount actually factored is not disclosed.

skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted (major): I re-read the pages they cite. AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.64 (cash flow statement): 'Increase in trade and other receivables (1,728) (1,624) (1,425)' and 'Increase in inventories (755) (131) (669)' for 2025, 2024 and 2023. Receivables also built by $1.6bn in 2024 and $1.4bn in 2023, so the 2025 build is the normal pattern. p.88 says the $2,681m FVOCI line covers customers 'that the Group has the option to factor, or relate to bank acceptance drafts received in settlement of trade receivables per common practice in China'. It is a classification and partly a China payment instrument, not proof of a factoring pool. The H1 2026 working-capital outflow grew to (1,438) from (771) (2026Q2 p.20). If 2025 had been channel loading that 2026 destocking unwound, that outflow would have shrunk. Combined with round 1 (destocking was a release bullet and a Q&A answer, and the CFO attributed the 2026 working-capital drag to the Farxiga loss of exclusivity), nothing non-obvious and true is left. But the pledge mixes manufacturing and R&D, and AZN already spends $14.2bn a year on R&D [p.F-2, page 61], so an unknown part is not incremental; comparing it to revenue overstates the new cost. The $440m is not a segment number (AZN reports one segment) and not a margin: p.F-22 says operating profit is that 'made by companies located in that area', i.e. a legal-entity figure after intra-group transfer pricing, royalties and wherever acquired-intangible amortisation sits. The same table gives the UK operating profit of 7,066 on external revenue of 4,359 (162%), which shows external revenue is not the denominator of entity profit; so 440/27,557 = 1.6% is not meaningful as a margin. The Americas also includes Canada ($954m) and other Americas ($2,633m), not only the US, and its profit swung 1,495 (2023) -> 423 -> 440, with a $213m pre-tax loss in 2025. Peer pledge ratios mix horizons (ABBV 10 years vs AZN 5) and come from force_summary.csv, not cited pages. Tariffs fall on the customs value of imported product, so the exposure base is the minority of imported product, not the $23.97bn US revenue line or entity profit. The pledge ratio (2.09x) is arithmetic on two headline numbers and includes R&D that AZN already spends. Correction: None that is material on cited numbers. The IP-regime tax angle (5.3pp of PBT, p.F-19) would need a sized ETR path to become a finding.

The angle that goes beyond a skim, profit booked in UK/Europe so a tariff taxes it, is contradicted by what management said plainly: Soriot, 2025Q1 prepared remarks, 'we currently have 11 manufacturing sites in the country, and the vast majority of our medicines sold in the U.S. are made domestically. We do import a minority of medicines' (grade C p.2); CFO Sarin, 2025Q2 Q&A to Peter Verdult, 'only a handful of products where we do import some products from Europe into the U.S... We will not be significantly impacted by tariffs' (grade C p.20). The Americas 1.6% segment margin reflects where IP and entrepreneur entities sit (transfer pricing), not the customs value of physical imports, so it does not measure tariff exposure. Correction: If kept at all, reframe as a tax point: onshoring production plus the UK/Swedish IP-regime benefit of 5.3pp (AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.78) means profit may migrate to a higher-tax US entity. That would be non-obvious only with a computed ETR effect; tariff exposure has been answered.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted (major): They are right that $440m is legal-entity operating profit ('made by companies located in that area'), not a segment margin (AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.81; AZN reports one segment). Their restatement, that about 89% of entity operating profit (UK 7,066 plus Rest of Europe 5,233, of 13,743) is booked by UK and European entities, is a transfer-pricing location. I checked whether that reopens a non-obvious angle. On tariffs it does not: management said plainly that the vast majority of US-sold medicines are made in the US and that only a handful of products are imported (2025Q1 grade C p.2; 2025Q2 grade C p.20). On tax it partly does. If onshoring moves manufacturing, and with it some entrepreneurial profit, into US entities, the UK and Swedish IP-incentive benefit of $655m (5.3pp of PBT, AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.78) is at risk. I found no release or call that links the $50bn programme to the tax rate. My round-1 searches ('manufacturing tax rate', 'tariff tax rate', 'transfer pricing') hit only the 18-22% guidance and Note 30 boilerplate, and 2026 Core tax-rate guidance is unchanged at 18-22% (2026Q2 p.1). The candidate as written (tariff on imports carrying group profit) stays refuted. Correction: Replace with a narrower tax angle: about 89% of entity profit and a $655m IP-regime tax benefit sit in UK and European entities, and nobody has asked what US onshoring under the $50bn pledge does to the 18-22% tax rate after 2029. This is non-obvious but unsized.

verdict_reason: Materiality held from r1 that entity profit over external revenue is not a margin (AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.F-22, page 81). Obviousness conceded that and showed management said the vast majority of US medicines are made in the US (2025Q1 transcript p.2; 2025Q2 p.20, grade C), which materiality accepted in r2. Both refute the candidate as written. Obviousness raised a residue (89% of entity profit and a $655m IP-regime tax benefit in UK/European entities, p.F-19 page 78, at risk from onshoring); it is unsized, nobody has asked it, and it is not the reader's claim, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than ruled a finding.

verdict_reason: Materiality verified Nexium's absence from 2026Q2 results pp.5-7 and 23-25 and its FY2025 size (AZN:reports/2025Q4_results_announcement.md p.7); obviousness found no release or call noting the change. Both narrowed to Nexium. On the disputed Andexxa reversal I opened the source: AZN:20f_FY2025.md p.F-29 (page 88) reports 'partial reversals of $407m Andexxa provisions previously recognised in 2024'; p.F-18 (page 77) shows the 2024 $480m Andexxa inventory and product provision was booked as a restructuring cost ('Other' restructuring, Cost of sales 569 in 2024), and the 2025 restructuring line is a net (138) credit to Cost of sales 'primarily due to the reversal'. Ruling: the reversal is not a valid sub-candidate. The charge sat in restructuring, which Core excludes, and the company attributes the reversal to the same restructuring Cost of sales line, so the $407m gross reversal is most plausibly netted there against other restructuring cost-of-sales charges; the obviousness skeptic's 'up to $269m in Core' has no page support. The net P&L effect the filing shows is $138m, about 1% of Reported operating profit ($13,743m) and zero on Core. Obviousness is right that it is unsaid; materiality is right that it does not move the investor metric. The Nexium change is a disclosure change with no earnings effect, so materiality is low even though the line is 1.4% of revenue. Surviving claim: Nexium, $831m of FY2025 Product Revenue (1.4% of Total Revenue, -5% at CER), was folded into Other Medicines in the 2026 quarterly tables without a reconciliation or comment; Andexxa and Kanuma are disclosed elsewhere and drop out of the claim.
